description: The ship-6 profile without the host KV tier, tp4/s6-notier: the ship-6 traffic profile (traffic-s6, unchanged and its waiver untouched, the rollback) less exactly its six host-tier lines, plus the text-only boot, as ONE traffic profile under ONE owner traffic waiver whose text carries the ship-6 waiver verbatim and says what it removes and adds (docs/tp4-s6-notier.md). The ship pack is generated by make_fusion_jobs.py (references/fusion-jobs/ship-traffic-s6-nt: B0 G1 GX0 GX1 G2 SR); its exactness control is the ship-6 profile.

ship.name: traffic-s6-nt
ship.reason: the ship-6 profile that serves production (traffic-s6, unchanged and its waiver untouched) WITHOUT the host KV tier (no QWEN_PREFIX_HOST_TIER_GIB, no complete spills, no tier verify or audit line, no sliced restore) and with the text-only boot (QWEN_C2_TEXT_ONLY_BOOT=1), the checkpoint store kept at 16 GiB, under ONE owner traffic waiver of its own: the owner's decision of 2026-11-17 to give the card host about 32 GiB of RAM back. Its exactness control is the ship-6 profile on the same image
ship.read_note: NO-TIER READ (tp4/s6-notier): no "host tier on" line and no "host tier restore slice on" line; the checkpoint store at 16 GiB; the "[PINDIAG] text-only boot: vision tower skipped" line once per engine process and no vision weight load in the boot log; the "[PINDIAG] host heap trimmed after warmup" line once (or its skipped line, never a traceback); every other ship-6 read unchanged (the governor's install line, WC's engaged line and its one octo decline).

waiver.waives: ONE waiver for everything the NEXT production candidate (tp4/next-1, the ship-5 candidate) carries that has no pinned qualification record. It carries, unchanged, every item the approved ship-4 waiver (ship4-fx-262k-2026-10-11, approved by the owner 2026-10-12) waives, EXCEPT the three changes (C2), (E2) and (L) named after it, and adds five levers, (G) to (K). THE INHERITED TEXT, verbatim from the ship-4 waiver: ONE waiver for everything this production candidate carries that has no pinned qualification record, each lever named with what it is outside of. (A) Inherited in full from w2-er-fx-262k-2026-10-11 (the approved fusion ship waiver, docs/tp4-fusion.md): the W2 multi SDPA launch (QWEN_FAST_TP4_SDPA=multi: outside packed_any_evidence_tp4_262144.json) and F1 (QWEN_FAST_TP4_CONV_GATES_SPREAD=1: no record), engine reuse and its drafter-trace book (QWEN_FAST_PARKED_ENGINES, QWEN_FAST_PARKED_DRAFTS: no ballast ladder, kill-switch drill or fault job), and the op-fusion levers (default-off, exact by construction and by audit on cards, no contract mechanism: named as the owner's decision). (B) The octo shape and its three levers, (1) QWEN_FAST_OCTO=live, the third packed block of eight users of eight rows (one 64-row verify pass instead of two M3 passes at eight live seats): its attention is the K64j extent program at flags 0x21 with one eight-row group per bundle (geometry G8B1), which is outside the pinned four-card evidence records (packed_any_evidence_tp4.json and packed_any_evidence_tp4_262144.json cover the served G8B2 programs at flags 0x23 and the multi-user launch is the M3 blocks' own), the batched GDN launch at eight users (96 cores, one wave) has no card-M record, and the serving_octo admission refuses the shape outside a gate run of a gate-only profile (QWEN_C2_GATE=1 with QWEN_C2_GATE_PROFILE=1) - this waiver is the one other way in, named by the profile's own QWEN_FAST_OCTO_WAIVER; (2) QWEN_FAST_OCTO_ATTN_BUNDLE=4, the octo block's attention in two K64j launches of four users per layer (flags 0x21 with B > 1 entries, 16 cores per entry, no kernel or factory change), outside every record; (3) QWEN_FAST_OCTO_GLUE8=1, the GDN split, merge, block conv and packed windows run by quarter-tile data-movement kernels at eight-row users (exact by construction and by the in-trace audit of the audited attach, with no card-M mover harness and no pinned record); (4) QWEN_FAST_OCTO_DRAFT=1, one eight-seat, eight-row draft pass in place of the two quads for an all-eight-live octo round (it can change only how many tokens a round commits (tau: its checkpoint is trained at sixteen rows), never which, and its trace beside engine reuse is not in the draft book: the coordinator rebuilds it after a rebound member); and QWEN_FAST_OCTO_MIN_LIVE=6, the eligibility knob. A record could replace this waiver: the K64j card jobs Q1w, Q1a and Q1b (k64j_card_b.py --kv-heads 1 --octo: G8B1 at flags 0x21 equal to its compile-time twin at every family and start, one trace over more than 50 families, the stale-writer zone and the native one-row decode against the one-entry call) with a bundle arm for B = 4 (not built), Q2 (gdn_tp4_card_test.py --users 8 --rows 8: one launch equal to eight per-user launches bit for bit) and a quarter-tile mover harness (not built), recorded in a new pinned section of the packed-any evidence beside the G8B2 one (not built); until then the owner's decision stands in for them. The op-fusion levers and QWEN_FAST_TAP_WINDOW_ALIGNED this profile also sets are the fusion ship waiver's kind (default-off, exact by construction and by audit, no contract mechanism) and are inherited from w2-er-fx-262k-2026-10-11 and named here as the owner's decision, not as a mechanism. (C) The host KV tier and the preconverted GDN checkpoints (QWEN_PREFIX_HOST_TIER_GIB=32 beside the 8 GiB checkpoint store, QWEN_PREFIX_CKPT_PRECONVERTED=1; docs/prefix-store-hygiene.md): outside any pinned record (the contract, prefix_policy_problems, admits them on a traffic profile only under a waiver naming each at this value, TIER_WAIVABLE_LEVERS); exact on cards on the gate-only audit twins, but the tier has run beside no concurrent decode of other seats, and never beside octo-T8, engine reuse's rebind of a parked engine on a restored turn, or the 16,500-block pool. The per-tenant quotas (QWEN_PREFIX_TENANT_QUOTA_*) are NOT in this profile: the contract refuses them on traffic (no qualification record exists) and the quota isolation gate TQ1 runs them on the audit twin only. (D) The prefill SDPA with one q chunk per core (QWEN_FAST_SDPA_PF_ONEQ=1): default-off, byte-identical to the stock path by the card-M proof and by audit; its binary K64j-OQ differs from the one the older packed-any records were made on and its OWN records have landed (RQ0-RQ2, all PASS), so a traffic boot passes admission; named here as the owner's decision. (E) The matmul grids for the 13x10 grid (QWEN_FAST_GRID13=prefill,drafter, M1): default-off, exact by argument and by audit on cards for the two sub-switches this profile names, the prefill all-gather matmuls and the fused commit's drafter feature projection. The third sub-switch, verify (the 64-row verify block's output projections, site verify.out), is NOT in this profile: its first audited attach (card run 38116769673) stopped at engine start before it compared anything, so it has never been audited exact on a card; it stays in the audited twin -s4-audit, whose next attach exercises and audits it, and adding it to the candidate (QWEN_FAST_GRID13=1) is a later decision after that audit passes. The decode ABAB of the grids (the F2 window) had not reported when this was written, so the line is the one switchable line of this profile: delete it from the ship entry of scripts/ci/fusion-wp/S4.json (and regenerate) if that ABAB or the N1/N2 pair shows a loss. (F) QWEN_FAST_TAP_WINDOW_ALIGNED=1 (tp4/rebind-fast: data movement only, bit-identical, removes a per-prompt-length compile on returning turns) and the tool-call whitespace fix (c2_toolcall_whitespace, a correctness fix, default ON for every profile, not a lever) are named as the owner's decision. Nothing in this list has run on a card TOGETHER: the audited attach A1, the ship gates and the tier pair of references/fusion-jobs/ship4 are the first CHANGES TO THE INHERITED ITEMS. (C2) The host KV tier is raised from the ship-4 waiver's 32 GiB beside the 8 GiB checkpoint store to QWEN_PREFIX_HOST_TIER_GIB=48 beside QWEN_PREFIX_STORE_GIB=16 (the whole prefix state's host budget: a 32 GiB share for the attention-KV pages and 16 GiB for the checkpoints, the budget the owner approved for this candidate; the preconverted checkpoints are unchanged: QWEN_PREFIX_CKPT_PRECONVERTED=1). The tier's mechanism is the one the ship-4 waiver's evidence covers; the size is the new number, and the larger checkpoint store is what the drafter-window carry (H) needs (each checkpoint then also holds up to 105 MB of window rows). (E2) QWEN_FAST_GRID13=1 in place of =prefill,drafter: the third sub-switch, verify (the 64-row verify block's output projections, site verify.out), joins the two the ship-4 waiver names. The ship-4 waiver held it out because its first audited attach had stopped at engine start before comparing anything; the ship-4 audited attach A1 (the audited twin carries QWEN_FAST_GRID13=1, all three sub-switches) has since compared it, exact on every audited round (the owner's reading: 4 of 4). It is default-off elsewhere and is the one switchable line of the candidate for this item: delete QWEN_FAST_GRID13 (or set it to prefill,drafter) in the ship entry of scripts/ci/fusion-wp/S5.json and regenerate if a timed pair shows a loss. (L) QWEN_FAST_OCTO_WAIVER names THIS waiver's id (the one name by which a non-gate run admits the octo shape and the lone-user round). ADDITIONS. (G) The lone-user padded round, QWEN_FAST_SOLO_PACKED=1 (NP1, docs/tp4-np1-fastlane.md): a lone live user (and a lone user of either M3 block) decodes on the padded 64-row packed block instead of its own 4-row engine; its third idle segment writes a scratch KV block the model's allocation adds past vLLM's pool (557,056 bytes a chip, idle_scratch.py). Gate-only until now (the contract refused it on a traffic profile and the admission ran in a gate run only): this waiver is the one other way in, as for octo-T8. No kernel, program or trace is new; what no card has done is give the K/V writers and the extent reader a block id past the pool in a page table (docs/tp4-np1-fastlane.md section 6, K1 to K4). Exactness is argued (the live segment's rows do not depend on where the idle segments write) and held by CPU tests; its audits run in the audited twin. (H) Exact resume P0, QWEN_PREFIX_STICKY_UNDROP=1 and QWEN_PREFIX_WINDOW_CARRY=1 (docs/tp4-exact-resume.md): a returning sticky turn resumes at floor2048(P) instead of floor2048(P) - 2048 (vLLM's last-block drop is lifted for the hit lookup, and the drafter window rows below the checkpoint are filed on it and uploaded on the resumed turn); byte-exact by construction (the same chunk-program checkpoints one chunk higher; the cold window's own rows), gate-only until now, never run on a card; the carry's audit (QWEN_PREFIX_WINDOW_CARRY_AUDIT) stays a gate's own and is in the audited twin. The turn telemetry that comes with it is on for every profile and counts only. (I) The sliced host-tier restore, QWEN_PREFIX_TIER_RESTORE_SLICE=512 with QWEN_PREFIX_TIER_RESTORE_SLICE_MS=200 (docs/prefix-store-hygiene.md "Sliced restore"): a returning session's blocks come back from the host tier a bounded slice per engine step, the one-fresh-prefill admission wrapper holding the returning request between slices so the other seats get a round. It moves no bytes and no answer, only when the work is done; the contract admits it on a traffic profile whose waiver names the tier (this one does). Never run on a card. (J) The drafter-window carry and the sliced restore beside the tier at 48 GiB: the three have never run together or beside octo-T8 or engine reuse's concurrent seats. (K) The Swift catalog entry's output ceiling, "output_budget": 32768 (NP9, docs/tp4-np9-answer32k.md), reaches every Swift boot of the image this candidate is built into: it is data in qwen_c2_checkpoints.json, not a lever of this profile (which keeps QWEN_FAST_OUTPUT_BUDGET=16384 and a default answer of 8,192 tokens), and it is named here because the candidate ships with it: it lifts the ceiling for a client that names max_tokens above 16,384 and costs KV admission for such a request (docs/tp4-np9-answer32k.md); deleting the key restores 16,384. (M) The device-side hand-off of the final prefill step's GDN state, QWEN_FAST_PREFILL_HANDOFF=1 (PF2-H, docs/tp4-prefill-2.md): the last step of every split prompt writes the decode slot from device-side clones of the B=1 prefill scratch instead of a host round trip (240 blocking reads, 240 uploads: 48.6 ms of device idle for the reads and 115.2 ms for the writes, 8.0 ms of it device kernels, in the ship-4 stack's device profile). A clone is a bit copy of the same tensor, so the bytes written are the scratch's; a clone that fails before the first write falls back to the host path (a logged line, never a failed request). Default off, never run on a card, and not a waivable mechanism of the contract (it is named here as the owner's decision, as the op-fusion levers are). IT SHIPS ONLY IF THE AUDITED RUN PASSES: the audited twin runs it with QWEN_FAST_PREFILL_HANDOFF_AUDIT=1 (the first 8 final steps and every 24th read the whole decode state before and after the write and require the slot equal to the scratch and every other row unchanged); a mismatch or a fall-back line in the audited run takes the line out of the ship entry of scripts/ci/fusion-wp/S5.json before the owner approves. (N) The lean admission, QWEN_FAST_ADMISSION_LEAN=1 (tp4/sched-1, docs/tp4-sched-1.md): a returning turn's engine rebind skips three admission costs after a slot's first adoption (the conv-slice read-back, the 'dram after engine' line, the post-prefill backstop's allocator read when the admission's own hold reading clears it by a wide margin); the first of each stays, the DRAM hold and the backstop's terms are unchanged. It returns device time to every decoder (ESTIMATE: the sticky build p50 541 ms to about 240 ms) and trades none away. Gate-only until now; never run on a card. (O) The complete spills of the host tier, QWEN_PREFIX_HOST_TIER_SPILL_MODE=complete (sched-1, with its default knobs): a flush no longer cuts the spill at 512 blocks and drops the rest for good (87% of a 254k restore's displaced blocks in the TC1 card run), so what the sliced restore (I) displaces stays in the tier; valid only beside the tier and meant to sit beside the sliced restore, which is why it is in this candidate; the step that displaces the blocks pays for the spill (ESTIMATE 0.4 ms a block once the slab is resident). (P) QWEN_FAST_ADMISSION_DIAG_TRIM=1, an existing flag the ship-4 profile does not set: the per-admission diagnostics after the first are not taken (about 100 ms of host time inside the admission freeze); named here as the owner's decision, not as a mechanism. The sched-1 governor knobs (QWEN_FAST_LEVERN_ADAPTIVE, _OWED_CAP_MS, _SHORT_SHARE, _SHORT_WAIT_S) are NOT in this profile: they trade decoder speed for first-token time and await the owner (their gate-only arm is -sch-all). The W3 levers (WC, the GDN windows, conv and gates in one launch) are NOT in this profile: they are in the audited twin only. NOTHING in this list has run on a card together, and (G), (H), (I) have not run on a card at all: the audited attach A1 and the prefix arm A2 of references/fusion-jobs/S5 are their first. || SHIP-6 (tp4/s6, docs/tp4-next2.md). THE TEXT ABOVE IS THE SHIP-5 WAIVER (ship5-fx-262k-2026-10-19, approved by the owner 2026-10-19 and serving production since), carried verbatim: this waiver covers everything the ship-5 profile carries on the terms of that text, and adds exactly the two items (Q) and (R). Where the text above says that the sched-1 governor knobs and the W3 levers are NOT in the profile, (Q) and (R) are the two exceptions, and only those two. (Q) W3 WC, QWEN_FAST_TP4_GDN_WC=1 (docs/tp4-w3-wc.md): the GDN layer's windows, convolution and gates in ONE launch (it replaces G3 to G8 of a layer, F1 inside) for a block of two or four users; the octo block (8 users of 8 rows) declines it with one logged line ("[PINDIAG] tp4 gdn wc fell back reason=8 users (WC takes 2 or 4)") and runs the shipped chain, so WC acts at two to four live seats only and gives nothing at six or more. Default off, not a waivable mechanism of the contract (named here as the owner's decision, as the op-fusion levers and PF2-H are). Its kernels were compiled for the first time in the ship-5 window's audited attach and held against the served per-user path on every audited layer of every M3 block: the audited twin (-s5-audit) carried it in two card runs with 0 mismatches over about 12,800 audited rounds; no TIMED run has carried it. IT SHIPS ONLY IF THE AUDITED RUN OF THE S6 TWIN PASSES AGAIN (WC and the governor together, 0 mismatches, no fall-back line but the octo decline) and the timed pair shows no loss. The line is the one switchable line for this item: delete QWEN_FAST_TP4_GDN_WC from the ship entry of scripts/ci/fusion-wp/S6.json and regenerate. (R) The adaptive Lever N governor, QWEN_FAST_LEVERN_ADAPTIVE=1 at its default knobs (QWEN_FAST_LEVERN_ADAPTIVE_DECODERS=2, _SHARE=0.9, _TTFT_S=120; docs/lever-n-adaptive-governor.md): while at most two decoders (and at least one) are live the alternator's base prefill share becomes max(profile, 0.9) and the deadline governor's target min(profile, 120 s); with none or three or more decoders live the very same calls run with the profile's values, so the pacing at the production load is today's step for step. Admission, step sizes and chunk boundaries are untouched and the decode-gap floor (QWEN_FAST_LEVERN_MAX_DECODE_GAP_S=8) is required and unchanged; the text of every answer is unchanged (only WHEN the decode rounds run between prefill steps moves). It TRADES decoder speed for first-token time: while a long prompt prefills beside one or two decoders those users get about a tenth of the wall time in decode rounds instead of half (ESTIMATE: their inter-token rate falls about five-fold for a window about 40 percent shorter) and the long prompt's first token comes sooner (ESTIMATE from the timing model, never measured on a card: -31 to -44 percent for a cold prompt of 32k to 254k tokens). Whether that trade is wanted is the owner's decision, and it is the second switchable line: delete QWEN_FAST_LEVERN_ADAPTIVE from the ship entry (and from this waiver's levers) of scripts/ci/fusion-wp/S6.json and regenerate. The contract admits the switch on a traffic profile only under a waiver that names it at this value (NEXT_WAIVABLE_LEVERS); its three knobs and the sched-1 pacing knobs (QWEN_FAST_LEVERN_OWED_CAP_MS, _SHORT_SHARE, _SHORT_WAIT_S) stay a gate's own. Built and unit-tested on the CPU (the port of tp4/prefill-1 into tp4/sched-1 and the tp4/s6 profile tests); NEVER run on a card, as a gate or as traffic: the first card run of it is the S6 window. Nothing in the two items has run on a card TOGETHER with the ship-5 stack's timed profile. || SHIP-6 WITHOUT THE HOST KV TIER (tp4/s6-notier, docs/tp4-s6-notier.md). THE TEXT ABOVE IS THE SHIP-6 WAIVER (ship6-fx-262k-2026-10-21, approved by the owner 2026-10-21 and serving production since), carried verbatim: this waiver covers everything the ship-6 profile carries on the terms of that text, EXCEPT the host KV tier, which this profile does not carry, and adds exactly the item (T). (S) REMOVED: the host KV tier and everything that only acts beside it. The profile sets none of QWEN_PREFIX_HOST_TIER_GIB (the 48 GiB host budget of (C2): a 32 GiB slab of attention-KV pages beside the 16 GiB checkpoint store), QWEN_PREFIX_HOST_TIER_SPILL_MODE=complete (O), QWEN_PREFIX_HOST_TIER_VERIFY, QWEN_PREFIX_HOST_TIER_AUDIT=0 and the sliced restore QWEN_PREFIX_TIER_RESTORE_SLICE=512 with QWEN_PREFIX_TIER_RESTORE_SLICE_MS=200 (I), and its waiver no longer names QWEN_PREFIX_HOST_TIER_GIB or QWEN_PREFIX_HOST_TIER_SPILL_MODE; where the text above describes (C), (C2), (I), (J) and (O) they are not in this profile. The tier off is the registry's default path and the contract's (no tier number, no spill mode, no slice: prefix_policy_problems has nothing to admit), so it removes a waived mechanism and adds none. Everything else of ship 6 is unchanged, the checkpoint store included (QWEN_PREFIX_STORE_GIB=16, the preconverted checkpoints, exact resume and the drafter-window carry (H), which lives in the checkpoints, not in the tier). WHY (the owner's decision of 2026-11-17): the slab is a MAP_SHARED anonymous mapping that never shrinks once written (no madvise or munmap, the kill switch only empties the free list), so after the first days of traffic it holds its whole 32 GiB of the card host's RAM for the life of the engine, and the engine's own counters show it restored NOTHING in five days of production traffic (tier_restore_requests 0 against 4,394 returning sessions served from the device pool and the checkpoints). What the removal can cost: a returning session whose KV blocks left the device pool re-prefills them instead of a host restore; the counters say that happened at most once (class_kv_evicted 1) in those five days. It moves no answer: the tier only ever restored digest-checked copies of blocks the prefill computes again. (T) The text-only boot, QWEN_C2_TEXT_ONLY_BOOT=1 (serving_c2_contract item 10): the profile admits no image and no video (limit-mm-per-prompt image 0, video 0, and batched serving is text-only by the wrapper's own assert), so the serving wrapper's call that builds the vision tower is skipped: no second from_pretrained of the checkpoint for its visual half and no vision weights on the device. A text request never reaches the tower, so no answer moves; the device DRAM it held is left free. Default off, refused by the contract on any profile that admits an image, and NEVER run on a card: B0, GX0/GX1 and SR of references/fusion-jobs/ship-traffic-s6-nt are its first. It is the one switchable line of this item: delete QWEN_C2_TEXT_ONLY_BOOT from the ship entry of scripts/ci/fusion-wp/S6NT.json and regenerate. Not a lever of this profile and not waived: the image of this branch also calls glibc malloc_trim(0) once after the fast worker's warm (serving_startup.trim_host_heap; host RAM only, never fatal, in every profile of the image).
